Task T5 is complete.

**Summary:**
- Wrote `out/T5/plan.yaml`: loads base (`model`) and adapter (`lora`) checkpoints, asserts 16 `lora_A`/`lora_B` pairs exist, computes `2 * B @ A` in fp32 via `matmul`+`scale`, accumulates into an fp32 copy of each base QKV weight via `cast`+`add_`, casts back to fp16, and `assign`s the result over the original weight name — keeping every write on the `model` alias so output-alias inference stays unambiguous (the `lora` alias is only ever read from, never written or deleted, so it's excluded from output).
- Ran it with `.venv/bin/brainsurgery out/T5/plan.yaml`: succeeded, wrote a 4-shard safetensors output (`out/T5/model-0000{1..4}-of-00004.safetensors` + `model.safetensors.index.json`), 244 tensors total, all shards ≤512MiB of tensor data.
- Verified independently with numpy: the 16 merged QKV weights match `base + 2·(B@A)` (cast fp32→fp16) with relative error ~3e-7 (well under the 1e-3 tolerance), unrelated tensors are bit-exact, no `lora`-named tensors remain, and layer-0 QKV weight shape is `[6144, 2048]`.
- One failed attempt along the way: tried to `load` the adapter into the already-existing `model` alias (to keep everything on one alias), which the provider rejects; fixed by using a separate `lora` alias and routing all destinations explicitly through `model::`.
- Wrote `out/T5/REPORT.md` with the self-report.
